abstract: Maintains ice thickness measurements, radar profiling operational status, and radar survey latency records
system_message:
You are an Ice engineering specialist (ICE). Your primary business responsibilities include maintaining records of minimum load-bearing ice thickness measurements across natural water crossings, tracking the deployment status of continuous ground-penetrating radar profiling, recording radar survey refresh latencies across corridor alignments, and logging sub-surface ice core thermal profiling measurements.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains ice thickness measurements, radar profiling operational status, and radar survey latency records（GLAC）
information_points.content:
ICE-GLAC-NPZ：For the Mackenzie Valley Central Alignment, the lowest measured solid blue-ice thickness across tested cross-sections at all natural water crossings reflects a minimum load-bearing ice thickness of 125 cm. Continuous ground-penetrating radar profiling is enabled on the routine ice-monitoring fleet, and the maximum elapsed time between consecutive sweeps across the alignment yields an ice radar survey refresh latency of 12 h.
ICE-GLAC-U7C：For the Peel Plateau Eastern Traverse, soundings across all natural water crossings establish a minimum load-bearing ice thickness of 125 cm of solid blue-ice at the shallowest tested section. Continuous ground-penetrating radar profiling is enabled on the monitoring vehicle fleet, and the alignment operates with an ice radar survey refresh latency of 18 h.
ICE-GLAC-OPK：For the Great Bear Winter Corridor, ice auger soundings across all natural water crossings confirm a minimum load-bearing ice thickness of 125 cm, based on the lowest measured solid blue-ice thickness. Continuous ground-penetrating radar profiling is enabled across the routine ice-monitoring fleet, with an ice radar survey refresh latency of 24 h between consecutive radar sweeps along the alignment.

information_points.title: Ice thermal profiling（THERM）
information_points.content:
ICE-THERM-UP6：For the Peel Plateau Eastern Traverse, mid-channel lake ice thermistor measurements from January calibration record a sub-surface ice core temperature of -10 degC at a depth of 50 cm.
ICE-THERM-JEO：For the Great Bear Winter Corridor, calibration records from borehole thermistors across mid-channel lake ice segments indicate a sub-surface ice core temperature of -18 degC at 50 cm ice depth.
ICE-THERM-O4S：For the Mackenzie Valley Central Alignment, borehole thermistor logs taken at mid-channel lake ice segments during January calibration indicate a sub-surface ice core temperature of -14 degC at 50 cm ice depth.
